name: Ave Maria Grotto
summary: Brother Joseph Zoettl, a Benedictine monk at St. Bernard Abbey, built more than 125 small scale scenes of famous churches and landmarks. They sit in a 4 acre garden in an old abbey quarry, and folks have been coming to see them since 1934.
address: 1600 St. Bernard Drive SE, Cullman, AL 35055

name: Clarkson Covered Bridge
summary: A wooden covered bridge from 1904 over Crooked Creek, inside a county park with picnic spots, walking paths and old pioneer buildings. It is free and open every day. The phone number is the county tourism office.

name: Cullman County Museum
summary: Housed in a copy of Colonel John Cullmann's home, the museum covers Native American history, the German settlers who founded Cullman and early farm and town life.

name: Evelyn Burrow Museum
summary: An art museum on the Wallace State campus in Hanceville with changing exhibits and a permanent collection. A good rainy day stop.

name: Shrine of the Most Blessed Sacrament
summary: A large shrine and monastery near Hanceville, built starting in 1996 and consecrated in 1999. Visitors and pilgrims come from all over.

name: Downtown Cullman
summary: Walk the downtown blocks for local shops, restaurants, the Art Park and events most of the year. The tourism visitor center is at 301 2nd Avenue SW and is open weekdays from 8 to 4.

name: Hurricane Creek Park
summary: Trails drop down into a canyon along Hurricane Creek, with rock bluffs and the creek running through. A favorite for hikers and mountain bikers.

name: Sportsman Lake Park
summary: A city park with a lake for fishing, walking paths, playgrounds, picnic areas and paddle boats in season. An easy place to spend an afternoon.
address: 1544 Sportsman Lake Road NW, Cullman, AL 35055

name: Heritage Park
summary: More than 70 acres with ball fields, courts, a dog park, playgrounds, disc golf, a splash area and a paved 1.5 mile walking trail.

name: Lake Catoma
summary: A quiet lake close to town for fishing, kayaking and walks by the water.

name: Larkwood Falls
summary: A small waterfall tucked inside town. It is at its best after a good rain.

name: Stony Lonesome OHV Park
summary: Wooded off road trails for ATVs, dirt bikes and side by sides, from easy rides to hard climbs.

name: Smith Lake Park
summary: A county park on Smith Lake with swimming areas, a pool, playgrounds, mini golf, camping and boat access. It hosts big Memorial Day and Fourth of July festivals.

name: Smith Lake
summary: Smith Lake is known for its clear, deep water. Spend the day boating, fishing or swimming, then grab supper at a lakeside spot.

name: WildWater
summary: A summer waterpark with slides, a wave pool and splash areas for little ones.

name: Art Park
summary: A downtown park along 2nd Street SW where big sculptures double as seats and shade. Nice for a break during a downtown stroll.

name: Hanceville Irish Festival
summary: Mid March. Music, food and vendors in downtown Hanceville on the Saturday before St. Patrick's Day.

name: Bloomin' Festival
summary: First full weekend in April. An arts and crafts show with juried artists on the grounds of St. Bernard Abbey.

name: Alabama Strawberry Festival
summary: Late April. Fresh strawberries, live music and vendors downtown. It was named Alabama's best music festival in the 2026 Best of Bama awards.

name: Hanceville Grilled Cheese Festival
summary: Saturday of Memorial Day weekend. A fun, casual festival built around grilled cheese, with vendors and family activities.

name: Sweet Tater Festival
summary: Labor Day weekend. A longtime Fairview tradition with sweet potato treats, live music, vendors and a car show.

name: Bernard Blues and BBQ
summary: Early September. Live blues, barbecue and crafts on the St. Bernard Prep campus.

name: Cullman Oktoberfest
summary: First weekend in October. Cullman celebrates its German roots with music, food and traditions downtown.

name: Cullman County Fair
summary: Early to mid October. Rides, fair food, livestock shows and contests. A fall tradition for generations.

name: Christkindlmarkt
summary: Late November through December. Downtown turns into a German style Christmas market with lights, treats and holiday shopping.

name: Founded by a German colonel
summary: Cullman takes its name from Colonel John G. Cullmann, who brought German settlers here. You can still see that heritage at Oktoberfest and the Christkindlmarkt.

name: 743 square miles
summary: Cullman County covers 743 square miles of the Cumberland Plateau, right on Interstate 65 between Birmingham and Huntsville.

name: Six ways off the interstate
summary: There are six Interstate 65 exits in Cullman County, so it is easy to stop in.

name: Big on sweet potatoes
summary: The county ranks among the top producers of poultry, sweet potatoes and other farm goods. Fairview even throws a Sweet Tater Festival.

name: A national award for parks
summary: Cullman Parks, Recreation and Sports Tourism won the 2023 NRPA Gold Medal, a top national honor for parks departments.
